messages:
PagerDuty: :rotating_light: Alert PD-9091 fired for service=runtime-kv-cache \u2014 symptom: p95 latency jump on kv:get (us-west-2)

maria.l: I'm oncall, ACKing. pulling dashboards and logs now.

jonah.c: saw a short spike ~30s ago, only in one AZ. no error rates. looks noisy.

maria.l: running `kubectl -n runtime exec deploy/kv-proxy -- curl -s localhost:9100/metrics | grep kv_read` \u2014 seeing bursty request latencies and a few warmup cycles.

robin.s: autoscaler shows a 2x spike in pod creations around that time. possible warm pool churn + a small set of long-context requests bypassing cache.

kevin.h: can we diff the routing logs for the affected minute? `gcloud logging read 'resource.labels.cluster_name=\"runtime-usw2\" AND timestamp>=\"2026-03-14T15:00:00Z\"' --limit 1000`

maria.l: pulled routing logs, here's a snippet: ```
route: /v1/generate model: rwd-large pool: ephemeral-small duration_ms: 1200
route: /v1/kv/get key: user:pref:123 duration_ms: 980
```

maria.l: looks like a few high-cost requests hit the smallest pool at the same time. bumped minReplicas for ephemeral-small +1 to smooth warmups.

incident-bot: runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/kv-cache-latency 

jonah.c: suggest muting the PD rule for 5m while we observe to prevent a pager storm. non-customer-facing so far.

robin.s: muting PD rule for 5m now. note: keeping escalation intact if error rate >0.1% persists.

kevin.h: temporary mitigation applied: routing tweak to prefer warm pools for requests with >1024 tokens: `route-priority: warm-first`

PagerDuty: PD-9091 -> status: triggered -> acknowledged by maria.l -> muted -> auto-resolved by monitoring after ~3m

maria.l: metrics trending back to baseline. p95 down from 1.2s -> 120ms. leaving the ephemeral bump for 10m to avoid bouncing.

jonah.c: root cause hypothesis: partner load test hammered a corner case, causing short warmup storms in a single AZ. no SLA impact; support shows zero new tickets. reached out to partner on slack channel.

kevin.h: follow-ups: 1) add 60s debounce to PD rule to reduce <1m flaps; 2) add ai-smoke that simulates warm-pool rotations; 3) ensure routing has a small guard against long-context to smallest pools.

maria.l: filing tasks and tagging eng-runtime + eng-platform. will monitor next 60m. thanks. :white_check_mark:

robin.s: unmuting PD rule in 4m. will keep an eye on alerts.

incident-bot: thread closed (auto-resolve). summary: brief kv-cache latency flare, mitigated via warm-pool min bump and routing preference; transient, no customer impact.
